questions.q: Which of the following would the TOGAF Standard accept as an 'enterprise'?
o: A group of geographically distant organizations linked by common ownership and shared goals
Only the IT function of a corporation
questions.e: An enterprise is any collection of organizations with a common set of goals; it may span partners, suppliers, and geographically distant units under common ownership.

questions.q: Which three architecture domains are collectively often referred to as IT architecture?
questions.e: Data, Application, and Technology are collectively often called IT architecture; Business is the fourth domain.

questions.q: In the TOGAF Standard, what is the primary use of abstraction when developing architecture?
o: To eliminate the need for stakeholder input
To divide a problem into smaller, easier-to-model areas
To store artifacts in the repository
questions.e: Abstraction divides a problem into smaller, easier-to-model areas (contextual, conceptual, logical, physical) that cross all four domains.

questions.q: The Enterprise Continuum comprises which two complementary concepts?
o: The Baseline Continuum and the Target Continuum
The Architecture Continuum and the Solutions Continuum
The Strategic Continuum and the Segment Continuum
The Foundation Continuum and the Industry Continuum
questions.e: The Enterprise Continuum comprises the Architecture Continuum and the Solutions Continuum, classifying assets from generic to organization-specific.

questions.q: Which part of the Architecture Repository holds the standards with which new architectures must comply?
questions.e: The Standards Library holds industry standards, supplier products, and shared services that new architectures must comply with. The Reference Library holds guidelines, templates, and patterns.

questions.q: In a gap analysis matrix, where is a Target ABB that has no counterpart in the Baseline recorded?
o: In the 'new' row, marked as a gap to be developed or procured
questions.e: A target ABB absent from the baseline appears in the 'new' row as a gap to be developed or procured. Baseline ABBs absent from the target go in the 'eliminated' column.

questions.q: Which sequence correctly lists the purpose of Phases B, C, and D in order?
questions.e: Phase B is Business Architecture, Phase C is Information Systems (Data and Application), and Phase D is Technology Architecture (BDAT order).

questions.q: Once a deliverable has been approved, how may it subsequently be changed?
o: It cannot be changed under any circumstances
Freely by any team member without oversight
Only through a change control / governance process
Only by starting an entirely new ADM cycle
questions.e: Approved does not mean finalized; approved deliverables may evolve but only through a change control / governance process.

questions.q: The ADM 'crop circle' graphic is best understood as which of the following?
o: A mandated activity sequence to follow in order
A stylized representation of essential information flows
A project schedule with fixed durations
questions.e: The graphic is a stylized path showing essential information flows between phases, not a process model, activity sequence, or waterfall.

questions.q: Regarding the Architecture Governance process, what does the Preliminary Phase do?
o: Operates the governance process day to day
Establishes the governance process and resources
Approves the Statement of Architecture Work
questions.e: The Preliminary Phase establishes (not operates) the Architecture Governance process and resources as part of building the Architecture Capability.

questions.q: What gate must be passed at the end of Phase A?
o: Finalization of the Implementation and Migration Plan
Approval to proceed with architecture development
questions.e: Phase A ends with obtaining approval to proceed, a critical gate before the domain architectures are developed.

questions.q: Phase C addresses the Information Systems Architectures. What does this include?
questions.e: Information Systems Architectures in Phase C cover both Data Architecture and Application Architecture.

questions.q: In which phase are Solution Building Blocks (SBBs) refined and delivery vehicles identified?
questions.e: Phase E performs initial implementation planning, refines selected ABBs into SBBs, identifies delivery vehicles, and determines Transition Architectures.

questions.q: Which pair of deliverables is finalized in Phase F, Migration Planning?
o: Statement of Architecture Work and Request for Architecture Work
Implementation and Migration Plan and the ADD
questions.e: Phase F finalizes the detailed Implementation and Migration Plan and the Architecture Definition Document, and confirms the Architecture Roadmap.

questions.q: What is the primary objective of Phase G, Implementation Governance?
o: To develop the Target Technology Architecture
To provide architectural oversight ensuring implementation conforms to the target
To identify stakeholders and their concerns
To decide between updating the architecture or starting a new cycle
questions.e: Phase G provides architectural oversight of implementation and ensures the delivered work conforms to the target architecture.

questions.q: A Change Request assessed in Phase H may lead to which two possible outcomes?
o: A light update to the architecture, or a full new ADM cycle
Cancellation of the enterprise, or a merger
Approval of the Vision, or rejection of the sponsor
Creation of the Preliminary Phase, or the Statement of Architecture Work
questions.e: Phase H is a holding phase; a Change Request may trigger a light update or a full new ADM cycle.

questions.q: Which statement about the Requirements Management phase is correct?
o: It connects to every phase including Preliminary
It connects to every phase except Preliminary and operates continuously
It runs once, between Phases A and B
It only executes at the end of the cycle
questions.e: Requirements Management sits at the centre, operates continuously, and connects to every phase except the Preliminary Phase.

questions.q: Who approves architecture principles once they have been developed?
questions.e: Architecture principles are developed by enterprise architects with key stakeholders and approved by the Architecture Board; they are altered through an amendment process.

questions.q: Which statement correctly describes the 'Implications' section of an architecture principle?
o: It lists the consequences of not following the principle
It states the requirements for Business and IT to carry out the principle
It is the short memorable label for the principle
It states the fundamental rule itself
questions.e: Implications state the requirements for Business and IT to carry out the principle, not the consequences of non-compliance. Name is the label; Statement is the rule.

questions.q: A principle that enables good-quality, consistent, and enforceable decisions even in complex or unforeseen situations satisfies which criterion?
questions.e: Robust means the principle enables good-quality, consistent, enforceable decisions even in complex situations. The five criteria are Understandable, Robust, Complete, Consistent, Stable.

questions.q: Good business scenario outcomes should follow which guidance?
o: They should be SMART: Specific, Measurable, Actionable, Realistic, Time-bound
They should be limited to Phase G
They should replace the Architecture Vision
questions.e: Business scenario outcomes should follow SMART (Specific, Measurable, Actionable, Realistic, Time-bound). Scenarios are used mainly in Phases A and B.

questions.q: How does the TOGAF Standard define interoperability?
o: The ability to store artifacts in a common repository
The ability to share information as well as services
The ability to run projects concurrently
The ability to comply with the target architecture
questions.e: Interoperability is the ability to share information as well as services; interoperability conflicts are reconciled as a step in Phase E.

questions.q: In TOGAF risk management, what does the 'residual' level of risk refer to?
o: Risk categorized before any mitigating action
Risk categorized after mitigating actions are applied
Risk that is impossible to identify
Risk transferred to a third party
questions.e: Initial risk is categorized before mitigation; residual risk is categorized after mitigating actions are applied.

questions.q: What does iteration within an ADM cycle primarily enable?
o: Projects to operate multiple ADM phases concurrently
The elimination of the Preliminary Phase
questions.e: Iteration supports projects operating multiple ADM phases concurrently, for example managing the B/C/D interrelationships together.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the three levels of the Architecture Landscape?
questions.e: The three landscape levels are Strategic, Segment, and Capability. Transition is an architecture state, not a landscape level.

questions.q: What is the guiding rule for how far to partition an architecture?
o: Partition until each architecture has one owning team
Partition to mirror the organizational chart
Do not partition; keep one monolithic architecture
questions.e: Partition until each architecture has one owning team, which gives clear responsibilities and avoids conflicts. The model reflects the enterprise operating model.

questions.q: Which of the following is one of the four dimensions used to scope an architecture?
questions.e: The four scope dimensions are Breadth, Depth, Time Period, and Architecture Domain. Segment is a landscape level, not a scope dimension.

questions.q: Governance is best summarized as a system by which the enterprise is:
questions.e: Governance is the system by which the current and future state are directed and controlled. Architecture Governance is part of corporate governance.

questions.q: Which of the following is a responsibility of the Architecture Board?
questions.e: The Architecture Board grants dispensations, enforces compliance, manages architecture contracts, and provides an escalation capability.

questions.q: Which document is itself considered a type of Architecture Contract, created in Phase A?
questions.e: The Statement of Architecture Work, agreed between the architecting organization and the sponsor, is a type of Architecture Contract. Other types include the Architecture Design and Development Contract and the Business Users Architecture Contract.

questions.q: When an Architecture Compliance Review identifies non-conformance, which of the following are the valid responses available to the architect?
o: Enforce compliance, grant a dispensation, or change the target architecture
Reassign decision rights to the architect
questions.e: On identifying non-conformance the architect can recommend three responses: enforce compliance, provide temporary relief via a dispensation, or change the target architecture.

questions.q: Which statement correctly describes the relationship between a view and a viewpoint?
o: A view is generic and reusable; a viewpoint is specific to one architecture
A viewpoint is generic and reusable and governs the construction of a view
Views and viewpoints are identical terms
A viewpoint is always expressed as a matrix
questions.e: A viewpoint is the generic, reusable lens defining conventions; the view is the specific representation built from it for a set of concerns.

questions.q: According to the TOGAF Standard, a stakeholder is best defined as which of the following?
o: Only the sponsor who funds the project
An individual, team, organization, or class thereof having an interest in a system
Any member of the Architecture Board
Only the end users of an application
questions.e: A stakeholder is an individual, team, organization, or class thereof having an interest in a system; in EA the system is the enterprise or part of it.

questions.q: Which statement about an Architecture Building Block (ABB) is correct?
o: It is a physical, deployable component
It describes a required capability and is supplier-independent
It is created only during implementation
It is a synonym for a Solution Building Block
questions.e: An ABB is a logical, supplier-independent description of a required capability that shapes the specification of the SBB, which is physical.

questions.q: Which deliverable is described as the quantitative companion to the Architecture Definition Document?
questions.e: The Architecture Requirements Specification is the quantitative view (measurable criteria) and companion to the ADD, which is the qualitative view.

questions.q: What is the primary purpose of the Communications Plan?
o: To trigger the start of an architecture cycle
To ensure the right architecture information reaches the right stakeholders at the right time
To contain the core architectural artifacts
questions.e: The Communications Plan conveys architecture information to stakeholders through a planned, managed process; it is created in Phase A and built from the stakeholder map.

questions.q: Which deliverable acts as a container for the core architectural artifacts and communicates the qualitative intent of the architecture?
questions.e: The ADD is the deliverable container for core artifacts and communicates the qualitative intent. The Vision is high-level and aspirational; the SoAW defines scope and approach.

questions.q: The Architecture Vision deliverable is best described as which of the following?
o: A high-level, aspirational summary of the capabilities and business value to be delivered
A container for all core architectural artifacts
questions.e: The Architecture Vision is a high-level, aspirational view and an early summary of the full Architecture Definition, used to communicate with stakeholders and gain early agreement.

questions.q: What is the key distinction between the Content Framework and the Architecture Repository?
o: The Content Framework stores artifacts; the Repository defines them
The Content Framework defines what work products to develop; the Repository stores the developed ones
The Content Framework is only used in Phase H
questions.e: The Content Framework categorizes and defines which work products to develop; actual developed work products are stored in the Architecture Repository.

questions.q: In which phase is the Architecture Capability first established?
questions.e: The Architecture Capability (roles, skills, responsibilities, processes) is established in the Preliminary Phase; its adequacy is later reassessed in Phase H.
